facts.raw_span: A 67-year-old man
hypertension, dyslipidaemia, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, active smoking (35 pack-years), a family history of ischaemic heart disease
prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina
exercise stress test induced angina at 50 W without ECG changes
normal sinus rhythm, Q waves in lead III, and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF
left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities
patent stents in the circumflex artery, non-significant disease in the left anterior descending artery, and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3
subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch
akinesia of all apical segments, later extending to mid-segments, hyperkinesia of the basal segments, and severely reduced LVEF of 35%
new QTc prolongation to 500 ms

concepts.why: The patient has a history of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction and presents with Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina, ST-segment elevation, and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis.
The patient developed akinesia of all apical segments, hyperkinesia of the basal segments, and severely reduced LVEF of 35% after a stressful event, consistent with takotsubo syndrome.
The patient developed recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation, requiring external shocks and cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

The patient has a history of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction and presents with ST-segment elevation and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis, consistent with myocardial infarction.
The patient has a history of hypertension, dyslipidaemia, and smoking, and presents with significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis, consistent with coronary artery disease.
The patient developed ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation, and has a history of abnormal ECG findings, consistent with cardiac arrhythmia.
The patient has a history of hypertension and presents with left ventricular ejection fraction of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities, consistent with hypertensive heart disease.
The patient has a history of stage 3 chronic kidney disease, which is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease.
it explains the uncovered finding of subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch
